title: Push vs Pull model: push notifications vs polling vs long-polling vs WebSocket vs SSE.
keyPoints: Pull means the client keeps asking (polling, long-polling); push means the server delivers on its own (WebSocket, SSE, push notifications).
Short polling is simple but wastes requests when nothing changed and adds latency up to the polling interval.
Long polling holds the request open until there is an update or timeout, giving near-real-time delivery over HTTP.
SSE (Server-Sent Events) streams one-way events over a single long-lived HTTP connection with auto-reconnect.
WebSocket is full-duplex bidirectional communication, ideal for interactive use like chat or live trading.
Mobile push notifications (APNs/FCM) reach a device even when the app is closed, essential for fraud alerts.
For millions of mostly idle clients, push notifications or long-polling can be cheaper than holding millions of WebSockets.

s1_definition.oneliner: Pull means the client keeps asking (polling, long-polling); push means the server delivers on its own (WebSocket, SSE, push notifications) : choose by latency, frequency, and direction.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Short polling** : the client requests updates on a fixed interval; simple but wastes requests and adds latency.
- **Long polling** : the client makes a request that the server holds open until an update or timeout, then reconnects.
- **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** : one-way server-to-client push over a single long-lived HTTP connection with auto-reconnect.
- **WebSocket** : full-duplex bidirectional connection where both client and server can send at any time.
- **Push notification** : platform-specific delivery (APNs, FCM) that reaches a device even when the app is closed.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh wants to know if his cheque cleared, he can keep phoning National Bank of India every few minutes : that is polling, the client pulling. Or the bank can send him an SMS the instant it clears : that is push, the server initiating. Polling wastes everyone's time if nothing changed; push delivers news immediately but requires the bank to keep a way to reach Rajesh.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Push vs Pull Spectrum

  ◄─── PULL (client asks) ──────────── PUSH (server delivers) ───►

  Short       Long        SSE         WebSocket    Mobile Push
  Polling     Polling     (one-way)   (bidirect.)  (APNs/FCM)
  ┌─────┐    ┌─────┐    ┌─────┐     ┌─────┐      ┌─────┐
  │ req │    │ req │    │  ←  │     │ ↔  │      │  ←  │
  │ res │    │wait │    │     │     │     │      │     │
  │ req │    │ res │    │  ←  │     │ ↔  │      │  ←  │
  │ res │    │ req │    │     │     │     │      │     │
  └─────┘    └─────┘    └─────┘     └─────┘      └─────┘
  Wasteful   Near-RT    One-way     Full-duplex   App closed
  Simple     HTTP-only  Auto-reco   Interactive   Platform svc

  Banking use cases:
  Balance check      -> Short polling (rare, latency-tolerant)
  Transfer status    -> Long polling or SSE (near-real-time)
  Live trading       -> WebSocket (bidirectional, fast)
  Fraud alert        -> Push notification (reaches closed app)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Push and pull describe who initiates data delivery, and I choose along that spectrum based on latency, update frequency, connection cost, and direction. Short polling is simple but wastes requests. Long polling gives near-real-time over HTTP. SSE streams one-way events over a persistent connection. WebSocket gives full-duplex for interactive use. Mobile push notifications reach a closed app.

At National Bank of India, each mechanism serves a different need. The balance check uses short polling because it is rare and latency-tolerant. Transfer status uses SSE for a real-time one-way feed. The live trading dashboard uses WebSocket for bidirectional interaction. Fraud alerts use push notifications because Priya must be reached even when the app is closed.

The senior consideration is connection cost at scale. Every open push connection consumes server memory, so for millions of mostly idle clients, push notifications or long-polling can actually be cheaper than holding a million open WebSockets. Matching the mechanism to both the latency need and the scale is what makes the delivery layer efficient.

Remember one sentence: use polling for rare updates, SSE for one-way real-time feeds, WebSocket for bidirectional interaction, and push notifications to reach closed apps.
